query: For high-entropy alloys intended for harsh corrosive mechanical environments, what single mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion, and why? Propose a controlled comparison that would test the hypothesis, predict how combined degradation and its wear and corrosion components would differ from a matched baseline, define where the prediction should hold or fail, identify supporting prior evidence, and state an observation that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: In high-entropy alloys (HEAs) exposed to simultaneous wear and corrosive attack, the selective segregation of passivation‐forming elements (such as Cr and Al) to wear-induced damage sites promotes a dynamic, self‐healing oxide film that reduces both mechanical wear and corrosion.
generation.material_initial_state: A multiprincipal-element HEA with a heterogeneous microstructure and an adequate concentration of passivating elements available for surface segregation.
generation.intervention: Expose the HEA to a tribocorrosion environment where mechanical sliding wear and a corrosive electrolyte (e.g., chloride-rich or acidic media) are applied concurrently.
generation.conditions: Harsh mechanical loading combined with corrosive conditions that mimic service environments (e.g., repeated sliding contact in an aggressive electrolyte at controlled temperature and pH).
generation.structural_mediator: The formation and persistence of a mechanically robust, multi-component oxide layer generated by the segregation of passivating elements at sites of wear damage.
generation.mechanism: Wear mechanically removes existing surface layers, instantly exposing fresh alloy substrate. In response, diffusion and selective segregation of Cr, Al, and similar elements rapidly form a protective oxide film that acts as a barrier to further wear and limits the electrolyte’s corrosive access. This dynamic re-passivation creates a synergy that lowers overall degradation compared to separate wear or corrosion events.
generation.predicted_outcome: Under combined tribological and corrosive loading, the overall material loss will be lower than the simple additive prediction from independent wear and corrosion tests. Specifically, the HEA will display a reduced degradation rate due to the self-regenerating oxide layer that mitigates both wear and corrosion concurrently.
generation.baseline: A matched test of the same HEA under separate wear and corrosion conditions or a variant HEA engineered with lower concentrations of passivating elements (thus with inhibited surface segregation) under identical tribocorrosion conditions.
generation.boundary: This mechanism should hold when the alloy composition enables sufficient elemental mobility and oxide formation. It may fail in environments where oxide formation is suppressed (e.g., in media containing aggressive species that dissolve oxides rapidly or at temperatures where diffusion is inhibited) or in HEA variants specially designed to limit segregation.
generation.uncertainty: The relative kinetics of oxide re-formation versus mechanical removal and the precise quantitative synergy between wear and corrosion mitigation remain uncertain; the magnitude of the improvement may vary with the specific alloy design and environmental parameters.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: (1) the standard HEA with normal passivating element content, and (2) a modified HEA with reduced passivating element content to suppress segregation. Subject both sets to identical tribocorrosion testing under controlled sliding wear in a corrosive electrolyte. Monitor surface evolution, oxide film formation, and overall material loss.
measurements: Surface oxide thickness and composition via X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) or transmission electron microscopy (TEM)
Wear rate quantification using profilometry or weight loss measurements
Corrosion rate assessment via electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) or potentiodynamic polarization
Overall degradation rate from combined tests versus the sum of separate wear and corrosion tests
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the standard HEA does not exhibit a significantly lower combined degradation rate compared to either the additive prediction of separate wear and corrosion or the modified HEA with reduced passivating elements, then the hypothesis is falsified.
